answer: A coastal economy stays honest when every new identity must complete a distinct salvage voyage to a different wreck, diving alone to recover one violet-marked relic from the seabed while a distinct harbour master watches the ascent, and logs the relic under one name alone. The first fake costs one voyage, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 voyages. Bulk farming fails because wrecks are few, each dive takes a full day, and one diver cannot surface from twenty wrecks at once, like a knoll that offers one safe anchorage per tide.
